protocol_type: Host-polled token / data / handshake transaction protocol; address-based (7-bit device address + 4-bit endpoint number).

channels.name: D+
channels.purpose: Differential data line positive. Idle state J indicates speed identification (D+ HIGH for FS, D- HIGH for LS).

channels.name: GND
channels.purpose: Common ground for the host, hubs, and all attached devices.

packet_classes.purpose: Host-issued; identifies the transaction to perform.
Carries the payload of a transaction.
Reports the outcome of a transaction.
Special transactions for HS hubs and bus management.

packet_id_field.structure: 4-bit PID followed by 4-bit complement (PID + ~PID) for single-bit-error detection.

transaction_phases: Token phase — host issues IN, OUT, SETUP, or SOF.
Data phase  — DATAx packet (host → device on OUT/SETUP; device → host on IN); optional for handshake-only transactions.
Handshake phase — receiver issues ACK / NAK / STALL / NYET (or PING outcome).

addressing.endpoint_zero_role: Default control endpoint; always present; bidirectional

transfer_types.use_case: Small data, bounded latency (1 ms FS, 125 µs HS)
Large data, best-effort, no latency guarantee
Periodic, guaranteed bandwidth, NO retry on error

control_transfer_stages: Setup stage — SETUP token + 8-byte DATA0 packet carrying bmRequestType / bRequest / wValue / wIndex / wLength.
Data stage  — optional; OUT or IN per direction bit in bmRequestType.
Status stage — zero-length DATA1 packet in the opposite direction of the Data stage (or IN if no Data stage).
valid_ready_handshake_rules: Host initiates every transaction with a Token packet.
Receiver acknowledges with ACK (success), NAK (busy / not ready), STALL (endpoint halted), NYET (accepted but next will NAK — HS only), or NRDY (HS PING flow).
Data toggle bit (DATA0 / DATA1) provides per-packet sequence numbering; only matched-toggle data is accepted.
SETUP token always uses DATA0 for the 8-byte setup packet and resets endpoint toggle.
